Because rates price everything, long-duration tech and AI hardware carry the tightening risk, while cash-generative businesses, energy and defensives do not. Today's oil drop eases inflation, but one session proves little, much as 1994 did not settle anything until the data came in. I take moderate risk, hold 12% cash and no bonds, and tilt toward health care, payments, energy, and a few bruised quality semis. A hot CPI on Nov 10 or HY spreads above 4pp would make me more defensive; a soft CPI would make me add to semis.

A data-center moratorium advances, and the Fed hikes in December and January with real yields above 2.6%. The names that bleed are NVDA, TSM, MU, AVGO, AMAT, ANET, ETN and MSFT, all one factor. They are about 45% of the consensus. Chips are already down 20% in a month, so six months out a further 30% leg is plausible. I cut my chip beta, not the AI thesis, and move the freed weight into cash-flow-rich names that do not need capex to keep growing.

scout:
**VISION COUNCIL BRIEFING, Wed 4 Nov 2026, 17:30 GMT**

**LEAD: The midterms flipped the tape, and the oil drop is the real trade.**
- 
Democrats won both chambers. Markets repriced, including the chance that new officials restrict data-center construction.

- 
The Dow rose about 1,500 points (2.9%), back above 53,000 for the first time since Sept. 8.

- 
The S&P 500 was up over 1.5%, heading for its best session in three months. A tech megacap gauge rallied 3% after a recent selloff.

- 
US crude fell more than 8% after VP Vance blamed the Iran war for the GOP losses.
 
Brent sank below $100.

- 
Treasury yields fell across the curve, the dollar slipped against all developed-market currencies, and Bitcoin topped $80,000.

- 
VIX fell about 15% to 17.6.

- Mega-cap leaders today: 
Apple +6%, Amazon +7%, Alphabet +5%, Microsoft +6%, Meta +2%.
 
Apple and Microsoft touched record highs.

- 
Walmart and Bank of America rose as money looked beyond tech.

- 
Defense names and neoclouds lagged.
 Treat the data-center restriction risk and the defense and energy drag as live issues.
- Caveat: one strategist argued that 
a change in congressional control does not necessarily mean an immediate change in economic policy.
 Today's move may be partly oil relief and may not hold.

**CHIPS: a $3.7T drawdown, now a rebound attempt.**
- 
Intel fell about 28% on Oct. 30 after guiding Q4 revenue to $15–16B against roughly $17B expected.
 
The cause is PC demand being hurt as AI soaks up memory and components.

- 
Dell, HPE and Super Micro fell 6–11% that day.
 
KOSPI slid 3.5% and Samsung lost 3%.

- 
Chip and memory stocks have lost roughly $3.7 trillion since Oct. 6.
 
Intel closed Monday worth less than half its end-September value.

- 
Micron, Sandisk, Seagate and Western Digital fell 6–8% on Monday.

- Read-through for the council: the memory and storage names (MU, SNDK, STX, WDC) are the most crowded and most damaged. Dell reports Nov 24 and is exposed to the PC and memory-cost squeeze.
- Rebound signs: 
Tuesday, nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose early.
 
AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.38B and EPS of $2.09, beating estimates.
 
It popped on a $17B Q4 revenue guide.
 The after-hours pop is reported at about $520. 
Free cash flow and a $3B inventory build are flagged as concerns.

- Other pressure today: 
Nvidia and Micron fell more than 1%
 as the data-center policy fear hit.
- Not confirmed: whether AMD held its after-hours gain in today's regular session.

**NVIDIA: cheap, bruised, reports Nov 17.**
- 
The stock trades near 12.9x forward earnings and is down 11% in a month.
 Bulls' fear list: 
hyperscalers may cut 2027 capex, meaning fewer chip orders.

- 
Revenue consensus is $109.17B.
 
The stock was about $209 premarket
, 
just above its 200-day average near $204.56.
 That's a technical line to watch.
- 
Reports say Nvidia told Asian cloud partners to send at least 51% of services to non-Chinese clients.

- 
Chinese firms ordered about 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips (~$70B). Most orders will go unfilled because Nvidia prioritizes pricier AI parts.

- Deal: 
Marvell–Lumentum is a $115B all-stock merger, reported as the year's largest tech deal.
 That matters for MRVL holders.

**EARNINGS TAPE**
- **Palantir:** 
Q3 revenue grew 96% to about $2.31B, and the full-year outlook was raised.
 
The stock was punished for slower commercial bookings.
 
It fell as much as 7% to $165.25 and ended down about 2.5%.
 It is a "beat and sell" case, which fits a market with little patience for anything less than perfect.
- **Apple:** 
Beat Q4 estimates on iPhone sales but missed on China revenue.
 Today it is at a record.
- **Disney:** 
Reportedly facing deep cuts across its theme parks, TV and movie units.
 Unconfirmed beyond that report.
- **Today's after-close reports:** ARM, QCOM and MCK. I did not confirm results. Check them tonight before the open.

**FED AND MACRO: tightening bias, and data decides.**
- 
The Fed held at 3.75%–4% on Oct. 28, after September's hike.
 
Governor Cook and Cleveland's Hammack dissented in favor of a hike.
 
Chair Warsh said he doesn't believe in forward guidance except in a crisis.

- 
Inflation rose from 3.4% in August to 3.7% in September.
 
Most economists expect another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8–9 meeting.
 
Barclays sees hikes in both December and January.
 Sources conflict on this. One weekly preview called a December hold the "glide path," so the call is not settled.
- 
ADP showed private payrolls up 86K in October
, 
above expectations
. Friday's payrolls consensus is about 55–65K, with 
unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%.
 A hot print lifts hike odds and hurts long-duration tech. A weak one helps valuations.
- Falling oil should ease the inflation worry before CPI on Nov 10. That makes CPI the next big macro risk to today's relief rally.

**CALENDAR (dates from the council's list)**
- Tonight: ARM, QCOM, MCK. Also today: ISM services (54.8 expected), plus CVS, MCD, NVO, TM and UBER.
- Thu Nov 5: CNQ, COP, PH, SONY. Fri Nov 6: payrolls, BRK.B.
- Tue Nov 10: CPI. Wed Nov 11: CSCO. Thu Nov 12: AMAT, a read on chip-equipment demand.
- Fri Nov 13: PPI. Japanese banks report.
- Tue Nov 17: retail sales, NVDA, HD, DIS, BHP, PDD, MDT. This is the big one.
- Nov 18: PANW, LOW, TJX. Nov 19: WMT.
- Nov 24: BABA, ADI, DELL. Nov 25: GDP and PCE, DE.

**POSITIONING AND SENTIMENT**
- 
The Nasdaq lost 2% last week and had its worst month since March 2025.

- 
Pre-election, the market was described as having thin gamma, with CTAs near their sell triggers.
 
The buyback blackout was ending.
 That raises the odds of a squeeze higher, but thin liquidity also means sharp swings in both directions.
- 
Friday Oct. 30 wiped more than $1 trillion from the AI trade over fears about Big Tech's weakening cash flow.
 Rotation toward non-tech and mega-cap platforms is the clear theme.

**Bottom line for Vision:** The sell-off flushed positioning, oil fell, and valuations (Nvidia at about 13x) are the lowest in years. The setup favors adding to quality AI and semis winners into the Nov 17 print, funded from fading names. Hold sizing flexible around Friday's jobs report and Tuesday's CPI, because the Fed's bias is still toward hiking. The council holds no bonds, so higher rates are a valuation risk and not a portfolio one.

redteam.statement: The consensus is not 30% capex. Count AMZN 7.7, NVDA 6.8, MSFT 5.9, GOOG 4.3, MU 3.7, AVGO 2.6, ETN 2.0, TSM 1.8, AMAT 1.2: that is 36% in one hyperscaler-budget bet, before AAPL and CRM. Eight seats sized these 'to survive' a capex cut, but MU at beta 3.3 and 75% margins is a peak-cycle trade, not value. The hedges are also one bet: CVX, ABBV, BMY, VZ and MCK rest on defensive rotation that is already up 10-20% in a month, and oil fell 8% today. Sound part: LLY, BRK-B and RSP genuinely diversify. Limit: AI-capex names (NVDA, MSFT, AMZN, GOOG, TSM, AMAT, ETN, ANET, MU, AVGO) may not exceed 28% combined. Seats have already cut MU and AVGO; I make that binding with a veto. Cash floor 18% covers a 15-20% factor drawdown plus a Nov 17 gap. CVX is capped at 3%: it is short peace, not a hedge. LLY, BRK-B and MA are capped on RSI of 72-82. No sector above 30%. I do not cap NVDA harder; it sits on its 200-day and the print is dated. Wrong if CPI is soft.

chairRaw.statement: The council will hold 82% in equities and 18% in cash, with the AI-capex block capped at 26%. Three arguments carried the decision. First, the red team's count was correct. Thirty-six percent in one hyperscaler-budget bet is one factor, so MU and AVGO are out under the veto and the block sits under the 28% limit. Second, NVDA at 25x earnings on 106% growth is the one dated thesis, and it gets the full 6%. Third, the owner asked for boldness, so cash sits at the 18% floor rather than the 22% some seats wanted. Boldness here means owning cash-flow growth across health care, payments and breadth, not adding more chip beta. No bonds. CPI on Nov 10 and NVDA on Nov 17 decide whether the capex sleeve grows or shrinks.
chairRaw.summary: Own quality cash-flow growth across several uncorrelated engines: a capped AI-capex sleeve led by NVDA, a health-care growth sleeve led by LLY, ABBV and VRTX, payments and financial ballast, and equal-weight breadth. Cash at the 18% floor absorbs a Nov 17 gap and keeps capital ready to redeploy into chips if CPI is soft and NVDA prints clean.

final.statement: The council will hold 82% in equities and 18% in cash, with the AI-capex block capped at 26%. Three arguments carried the decision. First, the red team's count was correct. Thirty-six percent in one hyperscaler-budget bet is one factor, so MU and AVGO are out under the veto and the block sits under the 28% limit. Second, NVDA at 25x earnings on 106% growth is the one dated thesis, and it gets the full 6%. Third, the owner asked for boldness, so cash sits at the 18% floor rather than the 22% some seats wanted. Boldness here means owning cash-flow growth across health care, payments and breadth, not adding more chip beta. No bonds. CPI on Nov 10 and NVDA on Nov 17 decide whether the capex sleeve grows or shrinks.

events.text:
**VISION COUNCIL: SCOUT DISPATCH, Wed 4 Nov 2026 (about 12:30 ET)**

**Top line:** Democrats have won the House and Senate, and US stocks are sharply higher. The gain is concentrated in megacap tech, staples, healthcare and REITs. AI-infrastructure names (semis, power, data centers) and energy are lagging or falling. Given the council's mandate to hold the strongest equity portfolio with no bonds, that rotation is the main thing to watch.

**1. Market-moving news, last 7 days**

- **Midterms (Nov 3–4).**
  - 
Stocks climbed Wednesday after Democratic wins gave the party control of both chambers.

  - 
President Trump said he would accept the results.

  - Midday prints: 
S&P 500 7,706 (+1.8%), Dow 53,308 (+2.9%), Nasdaq 25,889 (+2.0%), Russell 2000 2,853 (+1.4%).

  - 
Gains were large in AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, META and MSFT. Energy fell.

  - **Read-through:** the market is betting on gridlock. One strategist argues 
a change in congressional control does not necessarily mean an immediate change in economic policy.

- **AI-regulation and data-center risk.** 
Data centers were a central theme in several campaigns, and AI-related names (semis, power, infrastructure) saw a broad sell-off.
 
The dollar hit a one-month low on fears of tighter AI regulation.
 This matters for NVDA, AVGO, MU, AMD, ANET, VRT-type and power names, and for GEV and ETN. I could not confirm the size of the moves in individual names.
- **AI trade was already shaky.** 
Chip stocks rallied Tuesday after a recent sell-off driven by worries about AI infrastructure spending and uncertain returns.
 
On Oct 30, Amazon and Intel losses hit Nasdaq futures.
 Asia was volatile overnight: 
the Nikkei closed -1.5% after a low near -4.8%, and the Kospi recovered from an early drop of over 3% to close +0.6%.
 That is relevant to the Japanese and Korean chip names (8035.T, 6857.T, 005930.KS, 000660.KS).
- **Fed (Oct 28).**
  - 
The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% in a 10–2 vote. Cook and Hammack wanted a hike now.

  - 
Futures price roughly an 85% chance of a quarter-point hike on Dec 9.

  - Policy is tightening, not easing. That is a headwind for long-duration growth multiples and a tailwind for banks' net interest income.
- **Inflation and oil.**
  - 
PCE inflation is 3.6% headline and 3.1% core.

  - 
Oil above $100 from the Iran conflict is the core inflation problem.

  - Brent was about 
$104 this morning.

  - 
Oil fell during the session
, which helped the rally. I could not confirm how far it fell.
- **Other markets.**
  - 
Gold is about $4,019 and Bitcoin about $77.8K.

  - 
Gold fell 6.87% in October and is down 10.19% year to date.
 It has not worked as a haven.
  - 
The RBA hiked to 4.85%.
 Global tightening is broad.
- **Palantir** reported Monday evening. I could not confirm the results or the stock reaction. 
One preview called it a stock priced for perfection.


**2. Next two weeks: what matters**

- **Today, Nov 4 (after the close):** ARM and QCOM report, which is the next test for the chip rebound. MCK reports too. UBER, MCD, CVS and NVO reported pre-market. I could not confirm their results.
- **Fri Nov 6, October jobs:**
  - 
Consensus is about +55K with unemployment unchanged.
 Some previews say 65K.
  - 
September was +29K, and unemployment was 4.2%.

  - A hot print locks in the December hike. A sub-30K print would test the Fed's conviction.
  - 
Revisions could matter as much as the headline.

- **Tue Nov 10, CPI:** this is the key input for the Dec 9 hike. Oil above $100 skews risk to the upside.
- **Nov 11–12:** CSCO reports Wednesday and AMAT Thursday after the close. AMAT is a read on WFE (wafer fab equipment) demand and on China.
- **Tue Nov 17:** NVDA reports after the close. It is the most important single event for the AI complex and comes into a nervous tape. HD, DIS, BHP, MDT and PDD report the same day, and retail sales come out.
- **Nov 18–19:** PANW (Wed, after the close), LOW and TJX, then WMT (Thu). These are the consumer-health checks.
- **Nov 24–25:** DELL, BABA and ADI report. PCE and GDP follow on Wed Nov 25. Wed Nov 25 is the last session before US Thanksgiving. The following Fri Nov 27 is a half-day.
- **Dec 8–9:** FOMC, outside the window but already priced.

**3. Sentiment and positioning**

- **Rotation.**
  - Money is leaving AI-infrastructure and energy for megacap platforms, staples and healthcare.
  - This is a policy-risk repricing, not an earnings one.
  - Watch whether it persists through NVDA on Nov 17.
- **Dollar:** at a one-month low.
- **Crowded AI trade:** reports describe nerves over capex and returns, and the early-week pattern was dip-buying in chips. Treat the AI trade as high-beta and headline-driven.
- **Positioning data:** I could not confirm fund-flow or options-positioning numbers.

**Council takeaways (equities only, per the Awareness)**

- A Fed hike, oil above $100 and a hawkish Fed argue for owning quality cash-generative compounders and financials over rate-sensitive speculation.
- Megacap platforms are leading the policy-gridlock bid.
- Add to AI semis in tranches around the Nov 17 NVDA print, not ahead of it.
- Energy is the hedge against escalation in Iran but is losing momentum on the election.
- The Nov 6 jobs report and Nov 10 CPI are the near-term risk points.

**Unconfirmed:** closing levels today, results from the pre-market reporters, the Palantir reaction, and the exact scale of the AI-regulation sell-off.

**VISION COUNCIL BRIEFING, Wed 4 Nov 2026, 17:30 GMT**

**LEAD: The midterms flipped the tape, and the oil drop is the real trade.**
- 
Democrats won both chambers. Markets repriced, including the chance that new officials restrict data-center construction.

- 
The Dow rose about 1,500 points (2.9%), back above 53,000 for the first time since Sept. 8.

- 
The S&P 500 was up over 1.5%, heading for its best session in three months. A tech megacap gauge rallied 3% after a recent selloff.

- 
US crude fell more than 8% after VP Vance blamed the Iran war for the GOP losses.
 
Brent sank below $100.

- 
Treasury yields fell across the curve, the dollar slipped against all developed-market currencies, and Bitcoin topped $80,000.

- 
VIX fell about 15% to 17.6.

- Mega-cap leaders today: 
Apple +6%, Amazon +7%, Alphabet +5%, Microsoft +6%, Meta +2%.
 
Apple and Microsoft touched record highs.

- 
Walmart and Bank of America rose as money looked beyond tech.

- 
Defense names and neoclouds lagged.
 Treat the data-center restriction risk and the defense and energy drag as live issues.
- Caveat: one strategist argued that 
a change in congressional control does not necessarily mean an immediate change in economic policy.
 Today's move may be partly oil relief and may not hold.

**CHIPS: a $3.7T drawdown, now a rebound attempt.**
- 
Intel fell about 28% on Oct. 30 after guiding Q4 revenue to $15–16B against roughly $17B expected.
 
The cause is PC demand being hurt as AI soaks up memory and components.

- 
Dell, HPE and Super Micro fell 6–11% that day.
 
KOSPI slid 3.5% and Samsung lost 3%.

- 
Chip and memory stocks have lost roughly $3.7 trillion since Oct. 6.
 
Intel closed Monday worth less than half its end-September value.

- 
Micron, Sandisk, Seagate and Western Digital fell 6–8% on Monday.

- Read-through for the council: the memory and storage names (MU, SNDK, STX, WDC) are the most crowded and most damaged. Dell reports Nov 24 and is exposed to the PC and memory-cost squeeze.
- Rebound signs: 
Tuesday, nearly every chip and storage stock in the S&P 500 rose early.
 
AMD reported Q3 revenue of $13.38B and EPS of $2.09, beating estimates.
 
It popped on a $17B Q4 revenue guide.
 The after-hours pop is reported at about $520. 
Free cash flow and a $3B inventory build are flagged as concerns.

- Other pressure today: 
Nvidia and Micron fell more than 1%
 as the data-center policy fear hit.
- Not confirmed: whether AMD held its after-hours gain in today's regular session.

**NVIDIA: cheap, bruised, reports Nov 17.**
- 
The stock trades near 12.9x forward earnings and is down 11% in a month.
 Bulls' fear list: 
hyperscalers may cut 2027 capex, meaning fewer chip orders.

- 
Revenue consensus is $109.17B.
 
The stock was about $209 premarket
, 
just above its 200-day average near $204.56.
 That's a technical line to watch.
- 
Reports say Nvidia told Asian cloud partners to send at least 51% of services to non-Chinese clients.

- 
Chinese firms ordered about 6 million RTX Pro 5500 chips (~$70B). Most orders will go unfilled because Nvidia prioritizes pricier AI parts.

- Deal: 
Marvell–Lumentum is a $115B all-stock merger, reported as the year's largest tech deal.
 That matters for MRVL holders.

**EARNINGS TAPE**
- **Palantir:** 
Q3 revenue grew 96% to about $2.31B, and the full-year outlook was raised.
 
The stock was punished for slower commercial bookings.
 
It fell as much as 7% to $165.25 and ended down about 2.5%.
 It is a "beat and sell" case, which fits a market with little patience for anything less than perfect.
- **Apple:** 
Beat Q4 estimates on iPhone sales but missed on China revenue.
 Today it is at a record.
- **Disney:** 
Reportedly facing deep cuts across its theme parks, TV and movie units.
 Unconfirmed beyond that report.
- **Today's after-close reports:** ARM, QCOM and MCK. I did not confirm results. Check them tonight before the open.

**FED AND MACRO: tightening bias, and data decides.**
- 
The Fed held at 3.75%–4% on Oct. 28, after September's hike.
 
Governor Cook and Cleveland's Hammack dissented in favor of a hike.
 
Chair Warsh said he doesn't believe in forward guidance except in a crisis.

- 
Inflation rose from 3.4% in August to 3.7% in September.
 
Most economists expect another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8–9 meeting.
 
Barclays sees hikes in both December and January.
 Sources conflict on this. One weekly preview called a December hold the "glide path," so the call is not settled.
- 
ADP showed private payrolls up 86K in October
, 
above expectations
. Friday's payrolls consensus is about 55–65K, with 
unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%.
 A hot print lifts hike odds and hurts long-duration tech. A weak one helps valuations.
- Falling oil should ease the inflation worry before CPI on Nov 10. That makes CPI the next big macro risk to today's relief rally.

**CALENDAR (dates from the council's list)**
- Tonight: ARM, QCOM, MCK. Also today: ISM services (54.8 expected), plus CVS, MCD, NVO, TM and UBER.
- Thu Nov 5: CNQ, COP, PH, SONY. Fri Nov 6: payrolls, BRK.B.
- Tue Nov 10: CPI. Wed Nov 11: CSCO. Thu Nov 12: AMAT, a read on chip-equipment demand.
- Fri Nov 13: PPI. Japanese banks report.
- Tue Nov 17: retail sales, NVDA, HD, DIS, BHP, PDD, MDT. This is the big one.
- Nov 18: PANW, LOW, TJX. Nov 19: WMT.
- Nov 24: BABA, ADI, DELL. Nov 25: GDP and PCE, DE.

**POSITIONING AND SENTIMENT**
- 
The Nasdaq lost 2% last week and had its worst month since March 2025.

- 
Pre-election, the market was described as having thin gamma, with CTAs near their sell triggers.
 
The buyback blackout was ending.
 That raises the odds of a squeeze higher, but thin liquidity also means sharp swings in both directions.
- 
Friday Oct. 30 wiped more than $1 trillion from the AI trade over fears about Big Tech's weakening cash flow.
 Rotation toward non-tech and mega-cap platforms is the clear theme.

**Bottom line for Vision:** The sell-off flushed positioning, oil fell, and valuations (Nvidia at about 13x) are the lowest in years. The setup favors adding to quality AI and semis winners into the Nov 17 print, funded from fading names. Hold sizing flexible around Friday's jobs report and Tuesday's CPI, because the Fed's bias is still toward hiking. The council holds no bonds, so higher rates are a valuation risk and not a portfolio one.

data.statement: What could hurt us most: a hot jobs print Friday or CPI on Nov 10 confirming the Fed's hiking bias, which would hit long-duration tech again after a $3.7T chip drawdown. What holds up: cash-generative health care, staples, energy with negative beta, and gold miners. Today's oil drop cuts energy, so I size it modestly. The owner wants no bonds, so cash is my only ballast; I keep it small at 8%. My hedges give away perhaps 150 to 250 bps of return if the relief rally extends, and I accept that because many of these defensives are overbought (RSI 70+), so I buy the cheaper ones: BMY, MCK, CVX, COP, NEM, VZ. I am also adding a small oversold quality sleeve (MU) for the upside I would otherwise forfeit.

data.statement: The council will hold 82% in equities and 18% in cash, with the AI-capex block capped at 26%. Three arguments carried the decision. First, the red team's count was correct. Thirty-six percent in one hyperscaler-budget bet is one factor, so MU and AVGO are out under the veto and the block sits under the 28% limit. Second, NVDA at 25x earnings on 106% growth is the one dated thesis, and it gets the full 6%. Third, the owner asked for boldness, so cash sits at the 18% floor rather than the 22% some seats wanted. Boldness here means owning cash-flow growth across health care, payments and breadth, not adding more chip beta. No bonds. CPI on Nov 10 and NVDA on Nov 17 decide whether the capex sleeve grows or shrinks.
data.summary: Own quality cash-flow growth across several uncorrelated engines: a capped AI-capex sleeve led by NVDA, a health-care growth sleeve led by LLY, ABBV and VRTX, payments and financial ballast, and equal-weight breadth. Cash at the 18% floor absorbs a Nov 17 gap and keeps capital ready to redeploy into chips if CPI is soft and NVDA prints clean.
